Sundial — a desktop pet for Claude Code
=======================================

A small sun that sits on your desktop, showing the Claude Code sessions you
have running (what each is doing, how long the current turn has taken, how
much of the context window is used) and — if you have a Claude Max or Pro
subscription — how much of your usage allowance is left.

* An unofficial personal project. Not affiliated with Anthropic, and neither
  endorsed nor supported by them. The usage half relies on an undocumented
  endpoint and may stop working at any time.

Requires macOS 13 or later. Runs on both Intel and Apple silicon.


First, the important part: you do not have to sign in
-----------------------------------------------------

The app has two halves, and they are independent:

  · Session state and context consumption — read from local files on your own
    machine. No account, no subscription. It works the moment you install it.

  · The two usage dials — these need a Claude Max or Pro subscription.
    Without one, Claude's authorisation page simply refuses to connect. That
    is expected behaviour, not a fault in this app.

So: if you have no subscription, skip the sign-in step entirely. The sun and
the session blocks carry on working; you just will not have the two dials.

(The "or use an API key" option on that page does not help here. It is a
 separate billing arrangement, with no subscription-allowance figure to show.)


Opening it for the first time (please read)
-------------------------------------------

The app has not been notarised by Apple, so Gatekeeper will stop it the first
time. Either of these will do:

[Option one — least fuss]
Drag Sundial.app into your Applications folder, then open Terminal and paste
this line:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Sundial.app

After that it opens normally. You only ever need to do this once.

[Option two — no terminal]
Double-click it and let macOS block it. Then open System Settings › Privacy &
Security, scroll down to the notice about Sundial, and choose "Open Anyway".


Most people never sign in
-------------------------

If your Claude Code is the command-line one (the `claude` command in a
terminal) and you have already signed in there, Sundial simply reuses the
credentials it has stored — the two dials are there on first launch, with
nothing for you to do.

The next section only matters when that fails. The usual reason is that you
are using the Claude Code desktop app, which keeps its sign-in somewhere
Sundial cannot read.


How to sign in (only if the above failed, and you have Max/Pro)
---------------------------------------------------------------

1. On launch, a small grey sun appears in the bottom-right of your screen,
   dozing. With no session running and no sign-in yet, a small card appears
   beneath it with a "sign in" button.
2. Double-click the sun (or press that button). Your browser opens Claude's
   authorisation page.
3. Sign in to your own Claude account there and approve the request.
4. The page gives you an authorisation code. Copy it, paste it into the box
   that appeared under the sun, and confirm.
5. From then on it refreshes by itself. Signing in is a one-off.

   ! If the authorisation page says connecting Claude Code requires Claude Max
     or Pro, that account has no subscription. Signing in is not possible;
     skip it, and the session half carries on as normal.

   ! If you do have a subscription but sign-in keeps failing, the usual cause
     is an old authorisation tab still open in your browser, and a code copied
     from that stale page. Close all of them, start the sign-in again, and use
     only the code from the page that has just opened. Each code works once,
     and expires if left too long.


What you will see
-----------------

When nothing is happening there is just a sun on your desktop — no card, no
backing. That is deliberate: it takes up no room when it has nothing to say.
Hover over it and it expands.

Expanded, the sun sits in the middle with a ring on either side (subscribers
only):

  · Left ring (honey gold) — how much of the five-hour allowance is used.
  · Right ring (apricot pink) — whichever weekly allowance is under the most
    pressure. The label may read "weekly", or the name of one particular
    model; whichever is tightest is the one shown.
  · The sun itself — its mood follows usage. A broad grin when there is room,
    a flat line around halfway, a frown and a reddened body as the limit
    approaches. It also reaches its rays towards whichever side is tightest,
    swaying back and forth, with the tips glowing in that side's colour and
    growing brighter the fuller it gets. So even folded down to a single sun,
    one glance tells you which side is under pressure.
  · Below, one block per running Claude Code session: title, what it is doing,
    how long it has been running, and how much context is used. A session that
    is waiting for you to choose something jumps to the top.
  · Rest the pointer a moment and the full breakdown opens at the bottom.

A grey sun with its eyes closed and a few z's drifting off means there is no
session running. That is idle, not broken.


Controls
--------

  Drag            move it (the position is remembered)
  Double-click    starts sign-in if not signed in; otherwise refreshes now
  Click a block   dismisses its "finished but unread" marker
  Right-click     menu
  Hover           expands the breakdown; moving away folds it up

There is a small sun in the menu bar too, and it turns while a session is
running. Its menu holds: refresh now, sign in / sign out, show usage
breakdown, open the web usage page, clearer glass, keep above other windows,
launch at login, bring the pet back to the centre of the screen, and quit.

If you ever drag the pet somewhere you cannot see (easiest to do after
unplugging an external display), that last-but-one item brings it back.


What you need
-------------

· Claude Code installed — the session half depends on it, and that is the
  main feature.
· A Claude Max / Pro subscription — only the two dials need this. The app is
  perfectly usable without one.


Questions
---------

Q: The sun stays grey and still.
A: No running Claude Code session was detected. That is the normal idle state.

Q: What is the percentage inside a session block?
A: How much of the context window is used. When the bar turns deep red it is
   nearly full, and worth starting a fresh session.

Q: It keeps saying I am not signed in.
A: Without Max/Pro that is expected, and it does not affect the session
   display. With a subscription, double-click the sun and go through sign-in
   again — taking care not to use a code from an old browser tab.

Q: Do the figures match `/usage` inside Claude Code?
A: Yes, same source. It refreshes itself every minute; double-click to refresh
   immediately.

Q: Does it sit there eating CPU?
A: While a session is running, yes — measured at roughly a third of one core
   (28–37%). That is full-frame custom drawing plus a transcript poll every
   0.8 seconds. On a laptop it will sit fairly high in Activity Monitor. With
   nothing running it drops to a low frame rate, and stops entirely when the
   display sleeps.

Q: Does it upload anything of mine?
A: Apart from the one request that fetches usage (which only happens for
   subscribers), nothing is sent anywhere. No analytics, no crash reporting.
   The sign-in token stays on your own machine.

   The session half reads local files, and specifically: record types,
   timestamps, token counts, session titles, and the opening characters of
   your messages — the last of these to recognise the "interrupted with Esc"
   and "background task finished" markers. So the text of your messages is
   read into memory in order to test its prefix. It is not displayed, not
   retained and not sent anywhere, but saying the app "never touches your
   messages" would not be accurate, which is why it is spelt out here.

   Note also that session titles are shown on your desktop, so they are
   visible in screenshots and while screen-sharing.
